papers.title: Complex Intervention Frameworks for Acupuncture: Recommendations from a Scoping Review.
papers.authors: Guo ZY, Wang XZ, Hu XY, Hu XY, Tian ZY, Chen H et al.
papers.abstract:
To explore phase structures and evaluation components of existing complex intervention frameworks and to propose recommendations for future acupuncture frameworks.
Six databases and multiple sources of gray literature were searched. Literature on complex interventions, including guidelines, frameworks, models, methodological studies, consensus statements, policy documents, and web-based guidance, were included. A narrative synthesis was conducted to examine phase settings and inter-phase relationships. The included frameworks were further assessed for their applicability to acupuncture evaluation, and preliminary recommendations were developed.
A total of 46 publications were included, identifying 21 eligible frameworks, which were further categorized into 14 framework series. The included frameworks were mainly characterized by 3 phases, including preparatory, intervention evaluation, and long-term evaluation. Two evaluation approaches were identified, clinical-effect-first and mechanistic-first. Two structural design logics, sequential linear and sequential iterative models, were observed. The most frequently addressed phase components were overall effect evaluation (n=10, 71.4%) and component evaluation (n=13, 92.9%), whereas long-term outcomes were rarely considered (n=3, 21.4%). Regarding applicability to acupuncture, 4 major aspects were identified: acupuncture theory integration, individualized treatment adjustment, long-term follow-up, and real-world heterogeneity.
Existing frameworks vary substantially in phase structures and are not fully adapted to acupuncture. Potential considerations in future framework development include acupuncture theory and clinical experience, individualized intervention protocol, practitioner factors, acupuncture-specific outcomes, long-term follow-up and safety, and biomedical outcomes.

papers.title: In vitro digestion and fecal fermentation profiles of Cremastra appendiculata polysaccharide and evaluation of its antioxidant and hypoglycemic capacities.
papers.authors: Yu Peng X, Hu YB, Luo XL, Luan X, Yang Y, Li XJ et al.
papers.abstract:
Cremastra appendiculata is a traditional Chinese herbal medicine for liver cancer treatment. C. appendiculata polysaccharides (CAP) as a biomacromolecular showed significant lipid-lowering activities. However, the gastrointestinal metabolic fate and the bioactivities of the fermented products remain poorly understood.
Simulated salivary, gastric, intestinal digestion models, together with an in vitro human fecal fermentation system, were employed to evaluate the physicochemical profiles of CAP. Variations in molecular weight, reducing sugars, free monosaccharides, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), and pH were determined. 16S rRNA gene sequencing was performed to characterize alterations in fecal fermentation microbial communities, and the in vitro α-amylase and α-glucosidase inhibitory activities and antioxidant activities were assessed. As a result, during the simulated fermentation process, CAP remained structurally stable throughout simulated gastrointestinal digestion. During fecal fermentation, CAP was degraded by the fecal microbiota as the molecular weight decreased and the reducing sugars increased. Moreover, CAP significantly enhanced SCFAs production, particularly acetic acid and propionic acid, with a reduction in fermentation pH. CAP selectively enriched beneficial bacteria, including Bifidobacterium, Bacteroides, Lactobacillus and Odoribacter, while suppressing potentially harmful microorganisms, such as Proteobacteria, Bilophila, and Eggerthella. Furthermore, fecal fermentation of CAP enhanced inhibitory effects against α-amylase and α-glucosidase and antioxidant activities.
These findings provide mechanistic insights into the health-promoting properties of CAP and support its future development as a functional food ingredient and gut microbiota regulator.

papers.title: The bidirectional immunoregulatory effects of Traditional Chinese Medicine on the cGAS-STING signaling pathway and their translational prospects.
papers.authors: Yang Y, Sun Y, Cheng Y, Pan Z, Zhou J
papers.abstract: The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway is a central component of innate immunity, mediating host defense against pathogens, antitumor responses, and inflammation. Aberrant activation of this pathway is implicated in a spectrum of diseases, including autoimmune disorders, chronic inflammation, organ injury, and metabolic dysregulation. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), with its multi-component and multi-target characteristics, presents a promising strategy for modulating cGAS-STING signaling. Emerging evidence indicates that bioactive compounds, single herbs, herbal formulas, and related nanomedicines can bidirectionally regulate this pathway, either by directly targeting cGAS or STING or by influencing upstream processes such as DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release. These interventions modulate inflammatory responses, immune cell activity, and disease progression. TCM does not regulate cGAS-STING signaling through a single pathway alone. The cGAS-STING pathway interacts with NF-κB signaling, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, MAPK pathways, oxidative stress, autophagy, ferroptosis, and pyroptosis. These interactions may help explain the multi-target and multi-pathway effects of TCM in immune regulation. Here, we review recent advances in understanding TCM-cGAS-STING interactions, highlighting their roles in infection, cancer, autoimmune disorders, and other complex diseases, and discuss the mechanistic insights and translational potential of TCM in immune modulation.

papers.title: A Comparative Clinical Evaluation of Ultrasound-guided Acupotomy Combined with Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for Nonspecific Low Back Pain.
papers.authors: Zhang F, Liu L, Wang L, Chai D, Hu B
papers.abstract: Nonspecific low back pain (NLBP) is a prevalent condition associated with pain and functional limitation. This study evaluated the therapeutic efficacy and procedural feasibility of ultrasound-guided acupotomy combined with extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) compared with monotherapy approaches for NLBP. A total of 90 patients with NLBP were randomly allocated to three groups (n = 30 each). In the acupotomy group, trigger points within the lumbar erector spinae muscles were identified by palpation and treated using acupotomy. In the shock wave group, ESWT was applied to painful areas using an energy density of 0.10-0.20 mJ/mm2 at a frequency of 10 Hz. In the combined group, ESWT and acupotomy were performed sequentially under ultrasound guidance. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the visual analog scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and Japanese Orthopaedic Association (JOA) scores before treatment and at a 2-month follow-up. Therapeutic efficacy was additionally assessed in accordance with the Traditional Chinese Medicine Syndrome Diagnosis and Efficacy Standard. Baseline scores were comparable among groups (p > 0.05). After treatment, the combined group demonstrated significantly lower VAS and ODI scores, higher JOA scores, and a higher overall effective rate (93.33%) compared with the monotherapy groups (p < 0.05). This study presents a structured protocol for combining ultrasound-guided acupotomy with ESWT for NLBP and demonstrates improved short-term clinical outcomes compared with monotherapy.

papers.title: Targeting bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells with traditional Chinese medicine active ingredients: Restoring hematopoietic microenvironment homeostasis to prevent and treat myelosuppression.
papers.authors: Yan J, Qi Y, Guo J, Jiang X, Li J, Wan J et al.
papers.abstract: Myelosuppression is a common and dose-limiting severe complication in tumor radiotherapy and chemotherapy. The disruption of hematopoietic microenvironment homeostasis mediated by bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) may be one of the important pathological factors for its persistent non-healing. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) can regulate BMSCs function through multi-target and multi-pathway mechanisms, reshape the hematopoietic microenvironment, and support hematopoietic regeneration. This article systematically explains the network mechanisms by which BMSCs regulate hematopoiesis and the pathological mechanisms by which factors like radiotherapy and chemotherapy damage BMSCs. It explores how active ingredients in Chinese medicine can restore BMSCs function and remodel the hematopoietic microenvironment by regulating differentiation and enhancing paracrine effects, suggesting that shifting treatment strategies from "protecting the seeds" to "remodeling the soil" might be a promising direction. At the same time, it summarizes the potential application value of nano-targeted delivery to improve bone marrow homing efficiency of active ingredients and other new technology research progress. Although most studies are still at the preclinical stage, these findings suggest the potential value of TCM in treating myelosuppression and provide ideas and directions for using single-cell multi-omics to identify abnormal BMSCs subpopulations and their molecular targets, developing intelligent drug delivery systems, and conducting clinical translational research.

papers.title: Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu decoction suppresses experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis by promoting PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy and inhibiting microglial pyroptosis.
papers.authors: Li W, Wang S, Fang S, Ma W, Dou M, Yan T et al.
papers.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disorder of the central nervous system. Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction (HGWD), a classic traditional Chinese medicine formula, exerts protective effects against MS, yet the underlying mechanism involving mitophagy and microglial pyroptosis remains poorly elucidated. This study investigated the ameliorative effects of HGWD on experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) and its molecular mechanism. HGWD components were identified via UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap HRMS, and potential anti-MS targets were predicted by network pharmacology and molecular docking. EAE mice and LPS-stimulated microglia were treated with HGWD, with mitophagy inhibitor 3-MA and PINK1 siRNA used for mechanism validation. Assessments included clinical scoring, histopathology, Western blotting, immunofluorescence, ELISA, transmission electron microscopy and mitochondrial function assays. A total of 59 constituents were identified; network pharmacology revealed core pyroptosis-related targets (IL-1β, IL-18, NLRP3, CASP1) in MS, and molecular docking confirmed strong binding affinities between key active components and these proteins. HGWD significantly alleviated EAE clinical severity and reduced demyelination by enhancing PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy, improving mitochondrial function, and inhibiting microglial pyroptosis, which was validated in vitro. Notably, both 3-MA and PINK1 silencing abolished HGWD's protective effects. This study first confirms that HGWD treats EAE via the PINK1/Parkin mitophagy-pyroptosis axis, providing theoretical evidence for its clinical translation and quality control.

summary.methods: EAE 마우스와 LPS 자극 미세아교세포에 황기계지오물탕을 적용하고, 네트워크 약리학·분자도킹·조직학·단백질 분석·기능검사로 기전을 확인한 실험 연구다.
summary.results: 황기계지오물탕은 PINK1/Parkin 매개 미토파지를 촉진하고 미토콘드리아 기능을 개선하며 미세아교세포 파이롭토시스를 억제해 EAE 중증도와 탈수초를 줄였고, 3-MA와 PINK1 억제로 효과가 소실되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 전임상 연구는 황기계지오물탕의 MS 관련 기전 가능성을 시사하지만, 임상 적용 전 사람 대상 검증이 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 동물·세포 기반 전임상 연구이므로 실제 다발성경화증 환자에서의 유효성과 안전성은 명확하지 않다.

papers.title: [Research status and prospects of electroencephalogram characteristics in acupuncture for cognitive dysfunction].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wang X, Wu S, Yu H, Zhang Y, Zhang D, Li G
papers.abstract: To investigate the neuroelectrophysiological characteristics and current research status of acupuncture in modulating cognition-related brain functional activities, the paper reviews the recent electroencephalogram (EEG)-related studies on acupuncture for cognitive dysfunction. The review examines the changes in EEG features in this field from perspectives such as power spectral density, brain electrical microstates, functional connectivity, and time-frequency analysis. The results demonstrate that acupuncture can modulate abnormal brain electrical rhythm activities, improve the dynamic characteristics of brain electrical microstates, enhance functional connectivity in cognition-related brain regions,and promote the restoration of brain functional network activity to a relatively normal state. Based on the aforementioned research advancements, this study further evaluates the application value of EEG in identifying cognitive dysfunction at various stages and enhancing therapeutic effect of acupuncture, while it explores the potential of EEG technology in elucidating multi-scale neural modulation mechanisms underlying acupuncture and in developing personalized precision treatment protocols, aiming to provide novel insights and perspectives for advancing standardized research and clinical translation of acupuncture in the field of cognitive dysfunction.

summary.question: 침 치료가 인지 관련 뇌 기능 활동과 EEG 특성을 어떻게 조절하는지에 대해 어떤 연구가 진행되었는가?
summary.methods: 인지기능장애에 대한 침 치료의 EEG 관련 최근 연구를 주파수 스펙트럼, 뇌전기 미세상태, 기능적 연결성, 시간-주파수 분석 관점에서 검토한 서술적 고찰이다.
summary.results: 침 치료는 이상 뇌전 리듬을 조절하고 미세상태와 기능적 연결성을 개선하여 뇌 기능 네트워크를 비교적 정상 상태로 회복시키는 방향과 연관되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: EEG는 인지기능장애의 상태 평가와 침 치료 반응 탐색에 유용할 수 있으나, 임상 적용은 표준화된 근거 축적이 더 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 프로토콜 성격의 문헌고찰로, 원자료의 이질성과 근거 수준 한계로 인해 확정적 임상 결론을 내리기 어렵다.

papers.title: [Research progress on the regulatory mechanisms of inflammatory signaling pathways in acupuncture treatment for ischemic stroke].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Xia W, Li X, Han Y
papers.abstract: The occurrence of ischemic stroke is closely related to multiple inflammatory pathways, and acupuncture can improve neurological function in ischemic stroke by regulating inflammatory signaling pathways. At the level of pattern recognition receptors, acupuncture can inhibit high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1)/Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), NOD-like receptor thermal protein domain associated protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome, and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase(cGAS)/stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathways, thereby inhibiting excessive activation of innate immunity. At the level of transcription factors, acupuncture can downregulate pro-inflammatory signals such as nuclear factor-κ B (NF-κ B) and Janus kinase (JAK)/signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT), and activate protective pathways such as nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ(PPAR-γ), promoting microglial polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. At the level of kinase signaling,acupuncture synergistically exerts anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects by inhibiting the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway and activating the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt) pathway. Through coordinated regulation at multiple levels and multiple pathways, acupuncture systematically exerts multi-target anti-inflammatory effects, providing a basis for mechanistic research and clinical intervention in ischemic stroke.

papers.title: [Development and application of T-type thermocouple acupoint thermometer].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Ren Z, Zhang X, Xu W, Wu H, Zheng X, Zhou M et al.
papers.abstract: To address the limitations of existing acupoint temperature measurement, such as susceptibility to environmental interference, inability to perform dynamic monitoring, and invasive operation, a non-invasive acupoint thermometer based on T-type thermocouple has been developed. The instrument consists of multi-channel data collector,miniature thermocouple sensor, temperature-sensitive patch, and Toprie data processing software, offering the advantages including long-term dynamic monitoring of multiple acupoints, stable, rapid and accurate data acquisition, non-invasive portability, and ease of operation. Based on the Seebeck effect, the instrument uses a T-type thermocouple with the diameter ≤1 mm and thermal equilibrium time ≤1 s as the temperature sensing element. It enables long-term dynamic monitoring of multiple acupoints, thereby providing the objective quantitative data for diagnosis of traditional Chinese medicine. With the aid of miniaturization and wireless transmission technologies, the instrument is expected to be extended to clinical application scenarios such as chronic disease management, sports medicine monitoring, and health intervention of"preventive treatment of disease" in traditional Chinese medicine.

papers.title: [Experimental studies on acupuncture-moxibustion for irritable bowel syndrome in the past five years: a literature analysis].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Lin J, Weng Z, Zhang F, Zhou Y, Zhang Z, Lu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
To sort out the experimental research literature on acupuncture-moxibustion for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and to analyze the main research directions and progress of acupuncture-moxibustion for IBS.
Experimental research literature on acupuncture-moxibustion for IBS was retrieved from CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, PubMed, and Web of Science databases. The screening period was limited from January 1, 2020 to December 31, 2024, and data analysis was performed on all included literature.
A total of 124 articles were included, among which 66 articles were on diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D), accounting for 53.23%. The most commonly used modeling methods were chronic acute combining stress (CAS/CACS) and restraint stress combined with senna gavage in IBS-D studies, each being reported in 14 articles (each accounting for 21.21%). Electroacupuncture was the most frequently used [50.00%(67/134)]. The core acupoints were Zusanli (ST36) (78 times, 26.17%), Tianshu (ST25) (76 times, 25.50%), and Shangjuxu(ST37) (52 times, 17.45%). Visceral sensitivity was the most commonly used effect evaluation index [81.45% (101/124)]. In the past five years, studies on acupuncture-moxibustion for IBS have mainly focused on regulation of visceral hypersensitivity, regulation of inflammatory factors, regulation of intestinal flora, protection of intestinal barrier function,improvement of behavior and depressive symptoms, and regulation of metabolic disorders.
In the past five years,mechanism studies on acupuncture-moxibustion for IBS have achieved certain breakthroughs, but there are still deficiencies in the standardization of effect evaluation indexes and modeling methods. Future studies need to optimize the evaluation system, standardize modeling methods, and combine multidisciplinary approaches to deeply explore the mechanisms of acupuncture and moxibustion.

summary.question: 최근 5년간 과민성장증후군에 대한 침구·뜸 실험연구의 주요 연구방향과 진행 상황은 무엇인지 검토했다.

papers.title: [Academic perspective on a classic acupoint pair: Hegu (LI4) and Taichong (LR3)].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Chai Q, Liu B, Wang R, Li S
papers.abstract: Hegu (LI4) combined with Taichong (LR3) is a classic acupoint pair in science of acupuncture and moxibustion, widely recognized in academic circle as "four-gate points". Through conceptual tracing and textual research, it is determined that: XU Feng, the master of the Ming Dynasty, provided the annotations for Biao You Fu (Song to Elucidate Mysteries) chapter in Zhenjiu Daquan (The Complete Compendium of Acupuncture and Moxibustion), and he specified that Hegu (LI4) and Taichong (LR3) were the acupoints for "opening four gates". It is the beginning of the association between"four gates" and the two acupoints. However, these two acupoints were not commonly used as paired points by medical masters before that time. Medical texts of later ages further elaborated on this annotation, evolving the functions of Hegu (LI4)and Taichong (LR3) from merely "opening four gates" to encompassing both the concept of the "four gates" and the specific term "four-gate points". Even though, after specifically emphasized by XU Feng, this pair of acupoints had not been increasingly used in clinical practice. At that time, these two acupoints were primarily utilized in accordance with their respective therapeutic indications and their application was rarely guided by the theories such as "four gates", "four-gate points" and "opening four gates". Nowadays, the combination of Hegu (LI4) and Taichong (LR3) has been supported by the clear academic rationale. Such combination adheres to relatively rigorous principles of traditional acupuncture-moxibustion theories. Thus, it is concluded that theoretical construction and clinical practice do not represent a simple one-way relationship of "experience upgraded to theory". Academic research in acupuncture and moxibustion should distinguish between "the formulation of theories" and "the validation of theories", and it should be advanced prudently through both historical analysis and contemporary validation, so as to achieve a creative transformation of classical theories.

summary.question: 합곡(LI4)과 태충(LR3) 조합이 ‘사관혈’로 형성·정립된 학술적 배경은 무엇인가를 살폈다.

papers.title: [Mechanisms of moxibustion for delaying physical aging by regulating muscle-fat metabolism based on the theory of "Xieli Yinyang"].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Yang D, Zhang Y, Chen F, Yang Y, Wang Y, Wang Z et al.
papers.abstract: Based on the theory of "Xieli Yinyang", combined with modern studies on disease pathogenesis, this article proposes that the essence of physical aging is an imbalance of yin and yang, with muscle loss and fat accumulation as its major pathological characteristics. These two processes interact with each other, jointly leading to disorders of muscle-fat metabolism. Deficiency of yang qi is the key driving factor for muscle loss, whereas accumulation of yin turbidity is the primary cause of fat accumulation. Furthermore, moxibustion may regulate muscle-fat metabolism by reinforcing yang and replenishing deficiency to nourish muscles, warming the meridians and eliminating yin turbidity, thereby correcting ectopic fat accumulation and lipid metabolic disorders, improving muscle quality and thermogenic capacity, and enhancing motor function. These findings provide a novel therapeutic strategy for delaying physical aging.

summary.question: 뜸이 근육-지방 대사 이상을 조절해 신체 노화를 지연시킬 수 있는지 제시하는가?

summary.results: 근감소와 지방축적을 음양 불균형으로 보고, 뜸이 양기를 보강하고 음탁을 제거해 근육 질과 지방 대사를 개선할 수 있다고 제안하였다.

summary.limitations: 임상시험 결과가 아닌 이론적 제안이어서 실제 효과와 적용 가능성은 추가 연구가 필요하다.

papers.title: [A historical study of YANG Yiya's acupuncture writings].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wang R, Yang K, Gang W, Jia C
papers.abstract: The history of acupuncture writings by the Chinese medical scholar and educator YANG Yiya was systematically examined and organized. By consulting sources such as the Union Catalog of Chinese Medical Books and related bibliographical literature, we first compiled and verified the bibliographies of YANG's acupuncture works,correcting multiple errors in previous records and adding newly discovered works. Based on this, the study presents a chronological account of YANG Yiya's over 60 years of writing on acupuncture, closely linking his publications to his life experiences and the historical context. The study analyzes the background, content characteristics, and interrelations of his representative works. In total, YANG Yiya authored 27 confirmed acupuncture-related works, including textbooks,lecture notes, compiled works, translations, charts, journals, and monographs. This research holds significance for studies in the history of medicine during the Republican period, bibliographical research, and scholarly investigations of YANG Yiya's academic thought.
papers.title_ko: 양이야의 침구 저술에 대한 역사 연구

summary.question: 양이야의 침구 관련 저술과 그 역사적 맥락은 어떠한가?
summary.methods: 중의학 서지와 관련 문헌을 검토해 양이야의 침구 저작 목록을 대조·교정하고, 저술의 연대기와 특징을 역사적으로 정리한 서술 연구이다.
summary.results: 양이야의 침구 관련 저작 27종이 확정되었고, 60여 년에 걸친 저술 활동의 흐름과 대표 저작 간의 연관성이 정리되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 연구는 침구 임상효과를 평가한 것이 아니라, 근현대 침구 문헌사와 학문적 계보를 이해하는 데 참고가 된다.

papers.title: [Feasibility study on needle insertion with comfortable fine elongated-needles].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Fan W, Cui X, Zhao C, Shen W
papers.abstract: To meet the comfort requirements of contemporary acupuncture clinical practice, this study customized 8 specifications of fine elongated-needles, i.e. 0.16 mm×100 mm, 0.18 mm×100 mm, 0.20 mm×100 mm, 0.25 mm×100 mm, 0.16 mm×125 mm, 0.18 mm×125 mm, 0.20 mm×125 mm and 0.25 mm×125 mm. Taking the penetrating needling of bilateral Jianyu (LI15)-to-Binao (LI14) and Jianliao (TE14)-to-Binao (LI14) as examples, the practical feasibility of needle insertion was observed. The results showed that when using either the needle-holding insertion with both hands or the sectional tube-guided insertion, all specifications of fine elongated-needles could meet the clinical needling requirements, and all subjects experienced the deqi sensation characterized by soreness, numbness, heaviness and distension. The insertion depth of fine elongated-needles increased with the needle length. Compared with the needle-holding insertion with both hands, the sectional tube-guided insertion method was more capable of painless operation during skin penetration. This study provides a preliminary exploration of the clinical feasibility of needle insertion with the novel comfort fine elongated-needles, summarizes their operational characteristics and limitations, and may offer directions for further clinical validation.

papers.title: [Wrist-ankle acupuncture in treatment of chronic laryngitis based on "yang transforms qi, yin constitutes form"].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Xin S, Chen Z, Wang Z, Cai T, Zheng H, Liu J
papers.abstract: Chronic laryngitis is a kind of chronic inflammation of larynx characterized primarily by hoarseness. Its main pathological mechanisms involve insufficiency of yang for transforming qi and the internal production of phlegm-damp, or inadequacy of yin for constituting forms and yin deficiency of lung and kidney. The team applies wrist-ankle acupuncture under the guidance of the theory, "yang transforms qi, yin constitutes forms". The key operational principle of acupuncture is to stimulate the sites pertaining to yang when yang is deficient, while stimulate the sites pertaining to yin when yin is insufficient. The needles are inserted along the running direction of meridians that are distributed through the wrist joints. The therapeutic effect is determined by the changes of pulse conditions. When the needling technique of "yang transforms qi " is adopted, Yanglao (SI6) and Jiexi (ST41) on the left are selected; and when the needling technique of "yin constitutes form" is employed, Tongli (HT5) and Taixi (KI3) on the right are used commonly. The two needling techniques of wrist-ankle acupuncture are combined in treatment to ensure the satisfactory therapeutic effect on chronic laryngitis.

papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Zhou X, Wang R, Liu J, Xu Y
papers.abstract: Meige's syndrome is a refractory disorder characterized mainly by dystonia of the eyelids, typically presenting as blepharospasm and difficulty in opening the eyes, and may be accompanied by involuntary facial muscle spasms, with a prolonged and recurrent course. Professor YIN Kejing believes that the main pathogenesis of Meige's syndrome is internal stirring of liver wind. Treatment should address both the root cause and manifestations, with calming the liver and extinguishing wind as the general therapeutic principle. Professor YIN innovatively proposes the concept of alternative communication of the meridians, and adopts characteristic techniques including four-penetrating Yangbai(GB14), the double-needle connection technique, and the White Tiger Shaking Its Head manipulation to unblock the meridians, relieve spasm, and regulate qi and blood. The therapeutic efficacy is definite, providing a new approach for the clinical treatment of this disorder.

papers.title: [Refractory diabetic ulcer induced by recurrent herpes simplex treated with shallow lining-up fire needling therapy with filiform needle].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Sun W, Guo Y, Zhang M, Li J
papers.abstract: The paper introduces one case of refractory diabetic ulcer induced by recurrent herpes simplex treated with shallow lining-up fire needling therapy with filiform needle. In pathogenesis, the case was caused by damp-heat stagnation failing to heal the open wound. In treatment, 5 to 15 filiform needles, 0.30 mm×40 mm, lined-up, were burned and pricked into the wound quickly and shallowly; cupping was combined. This therapy was operated once every 3 days, twice weekly.The incrustation was presented on the wound after 3 days of first treatment. The ulcer was significantly reduced in size with new granulation tissue formed after 2 weeks of treatment. The wound was completely healed, only with pigmentation left after 3 weeks of treatment. During treatment, blood glucose level decreased steadily. No recurrence was observed during one-month follow-up. This case demonstrates the unique advantages of fire needling therapy with filiform needle in treatment of refractory wound, providing a safe and effective therapeutic approach to relevant conditions with traditional Chinese medicine.

papers.title: [Clinical experience in treatment of dysmyotonia with the combination of acupuncture and herbal medicine based on the theory of "kidney deficiency, impairment of governor vessel and meridian damage by toxin"].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Huang D, Wang C, Chen Z, Li B, Wang S, Li X et al.
papers.abstract: Based on the theory of "kidney deficiency, impairment of governor vessel and meridian damage by toxin", it is pointed that the core pathogenesis of dysmyotonia lies in deficiency of the spleen and kidney and malnutrition of the governor vessel, complicated with the invasion of pathogens such as wind, fire, phlegm, stasis and toxin (especially drug toxin) to the body, as well as meridian damage by toxin. The combination of acupuncture and herbal medicine is adopted in treatment.Acupuncture focuses on regulating the governor vessel and filling up the sea of marrow. The acupoints of the governor vessel and back-shu points are the primary, in association with the acupoints selected according to meridian differentiation, and the theories of biaoben genjie and sihai qijie, as well as the modern anatomical theory. Herbal medicine is administered in line with syndrome differentiation and pathogenesis to address both symptoms and root cause simultaneously. In treatment, moxibustion is operated to warm yang, and daoyin is to regulate qi specially, so as to provide a holistic regimen for mental and physical adjustment. This treatment modality employs multi-target interventions by regulating qi flow,eliminating pathogenic factors and detoxifying, harmonizing zangfu, and replenishing essence and marrow; and provides safe and effective strategy for optimizing the diagnosis and treatment of TCM for dysmyotonia by integrating with modern neural modulation mechanism.

papers.title: [Biomechanical effect of acupotomy on cartilage degeneration in rabbits with knee osteoarthritis].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Sun L, Zhu X, Gao H, Zhang Y, Shao X, Wang R et al.
papers.abstract:
To observe the effects of acupotomy on the biomechanical characteristics and cartilage degeneration of knee joint in rabbits with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) , and to explore the therapeutic mechanism of acupotomy in treatment of KOA.
Twenty-four 6-month-old male New Zealand rabbits were randomly assigned to a normal group, a model group and an acupotomy group, 8 rabbits in each group. Except the normal group, all other groups underwent the modified Videman method to induce KOA by immobilizing the left hind limb in extension for 6 weeks. In the acupotomy group, acupotomy was operated at the left knee on the tendon insertions of the vastus medialis, vastus lateralis, rectus femoris,and biceps femoris, and on the pes anserine bursa, once a week for 3 weeks. Before and after intervention, the score of Lequesne MG and passive range of motion (PROM) were observed in the knee joint of the rabbit's left hind limb. After intervention completion, the root mean square (RMS) of surface electromyographic signals from the flexor and extensor muscle groups of the knee joint of the rabbit's left hind limb was evaluated, the knee joint force exerted by the left hind limb at the moment of takeoff was collected. Immunofluorescence staining was used to detect the fluorescence intensity of type Ⅱcollagen (Col-Ⅱ) in the knee cartilage of rabbit left hind limb, while ELISA was employed to determine the levels of cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP) and type Ⅱ collagen carboxyl-terminal peptide (CTX-Ⅱ) in rabbit serum.
After intervention, compared with the normal group, the model group showed the increase in the Lequesne MG score (P<0.05),and the decrease in PROM, RMS of the flexor and extensor muscle groups, knee joint force of the left hind limb, fluorescence intensity of Col-Ⅱ in the cartilage of the knee joint of the left hind limb (P<0.05), and the elevation in serum COMP and CTX-Ⅱ(P<0.05). When compared with the model group, the acupotomy group exhibited the decrease in the Lequesne MG score (P<0.05), and the increase in PROM, RMS in the flexor and extensor muscle groups, knee joint force of the left hind limb, fluorescence intensity of Col-Ⅱ in cartilage of the knee joint of the left hind limb (P<0.05), and the decline of serum COMP and CTX-Ⅱ(P<0.05).
Acupotomy can retard cartilage degeneration in KOA by modulating the activation of flexor and extensor muscle groups of knee joint, strengthening knee joint force, and suppressing extracellular matrix degradation.

papers.title: [Effect of electroacupuncture on microglial activation in the lumbar spinal cord of rabbits with lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Yang J, Liu Y
papers.abstract:
To explore the effects of electroacupuncture (EA) on microglial activation in the lumbar spinal cord and the ultrastructure of intervertebral disc nucleus pulposus cells in rabbits with lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (LIDD).
Twenty-four SPF-grade healthy male New Zealand rabbits were randomly divided into a control group, a sham operation group, a degeneration group, and an EA group, with 6 rabbits in each group. The degeneration group and the EA group were treated with annulus fibrosus injury method to establish LIDD models. The EA group was treated with EA intervention at bilateral L4 and L5 Jiaji (EX-B2) points, with disperse-dense wave, frequency in 2 Hz/15 Hz, 20 min each time, once daily, with 6 consecutive days followed by 1 day of rest, for 4 weeks. Gait function and Pfirrmann grading scores were compared among groups. Immunohistochemistry was used to detect positive expression of the microglial markers Oxford 42 (OX42) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX2) in the dorsal horn of the lumbar spinal cord. ELISA was used to detect the levels of inflammatory factors (tumor necrosis factor-α [TNF-α], interleukin [IL]-1β, IL-6, and IL-10) in the lumbar spinal cord. Transmission electron microscopy was used to observe the ultrastructure of nucleus pulposus cells of lumbar intervertebral discs. Western blot was used to detect protein expression of aggrecan and collagen Ⅱ in the nucleus pulposus of lumbar intervertebral discs in each group.
Compared with the control group, there were no statistically significant differences in gait function score, Pfirrmann grading score, mean optical density values of OX42 and COX2 in the dorsal horn of the lumbar spinal cord, levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-10 in the lumbar spinal cord, and protein expression of aggrecan and collagen Ⅱ in the nucleus pulposus of lumbar intervertebral discs in the sham operation group(P>0.05). Compared with the sham operation group, the degeneration group showed decreased gait function score (P<0.05)and increased Pfirrmann grading score (P<0.05); the mean optical density values of OX42 and COX2 in the dorsal horn of the lumbar spinal cord were increased (P<0.05); the levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 in the lumbar spinal cord were increased (P<0.05), while the level of IL-10 was decreased (P<0.05); nucleus pulposus cells of lumbar intervertebral discs showed irregular cell membranes, nuclear pyknosis, cytoplasmic condensation, decreased organelles in the cytoplasm, and mitochondrial swelling or vacuolization; protein expression of aggrecan and collagen Ⅱ in the nucleus pulposus of lumbar intervertebral discs was decreased (P<0.05). Compared with the degeneration group, the EA group showed increased gait function score (P<0.05) and decreased Pfirrmann grading score (P<0.05); the mean optical density values of OX42 and COX2 in the dorsal horn of the lumbar spinal cord were decreased (P<0.05); the levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 in the lumbar spinal cord were decreased (P<0.05), while the level of IL-10 was increased (P<0.05); irregular cell membranes, nuclear pyknosis, and cytoplasmic condensation of nucleus pulposus cells of lumbar intervertebral discs were obviously improved, cytoplasmic organelles were relatively complete, and mitochondria showed mild swelling;protein expression of aggrecan and collagen Ⅱ in the nucleus pulposus of lumbar intervertebral discs was increased(P<0.05).
EA may alleviate intervertebral disc degeneration by inhibiting microglial activation and its inflammatory response in the lumbar spinal cord of LIDD model rabbits, and improving the ultrastructure of intervertebral disc nucleus pulposus cells.

papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Zhuo Y, Wu Z, Luo Y, Huang X, Rao X, Wu J
papers.abstract:
To observe the efficacy of "Tiaojing Cuyun Acupuncture" combined with hormone replacement therapy in the treatment of premature ovarian failure (POF), and to investigate differences in vaginal microbiota among patients with different therapeutic responses, thereby preliminarily exploring the mechanism underlying efficacy differences.
Ninety-eight patients with POF were randomly divided into an observation group (49 cases, 1 case was eliminated)and a control group (49 cases, 1 case dropped out). The control group was treated with hormone replacement therapy with Femoston, one tablet each time, once daily. On the basis of the control group, the observation group was additionally treated with "Tiaojing Cuyun Acupuncture". Acupoint group 1 included Baihui (GV20), Zhongwan (CV12), Guanyuan (CV4), and bilateral Tianshu (ST25), Zigong (EX-CA1), Dahe (KI12), Zusanli (ST36), Sanyinjiao (SP6), and Taichong (LR3). Acupoint group 2 included Baihui (GV20), bilateral Shenshu (BL23), Ciliao (BL32), and Taixi (KI3). The two acupoint groups were used alternately, beginning with acupoint group 1. Treatment was administered once every other day, three times per week.Both groups were treated for three menstrual cycles. Serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH),estradiol (E2), and anti-M ü llerian hormone (AMH) levels on days 3-5 of the menstrual cycle were measured before and after treatment in the two groups. Self-rating anxiety scale (SAS) scores were assessed before and after treatment, and clinical efficacy was evaluated in the two groups. Five effective patients (G0 subgroup) and five ineffective patients (G1 subgroup)were randomly selected from each group, and their vaginal microbiota structure was analyzed using 16S rRNA sequencing.
After treatment, FSH levels in both groups were lower than those before treatment (P<0.05); SAS scores in both groups were lower than those before treatment (P<0.05), and the observation group had lower SAS score than the control group (P<0.05). The total effective rate was 77.1% (37/48) in the observation group, which was higher than 56.3% (27/48) in the control group (P<0.05). Vaginal microbiota analysis showed that at the phylum level, the relative abundance of Firmicutes in the G0 subgroup of the control group was higher than that in the G1 subgroup, while the relative abundances of Bacteroidetes, Actinobacteria and Proteobacteria were lowed in the G0 subgroup. In contrast, the observation group exhibited an opposite trend: the G0 subgroup had lower Firmicutes abundance but higher abundances of Actinobacteria, Bacteroidetes and Proteobacteria compared with the G1 subgroup. At the family and genus levels, Bifidobacterium was enriched in the G0 subgroups of both groups, whereas Lactobacillus predominated in the G1 subgroups. The G0 subgroup of the control group showed higher abundance of Gardnerella, while both Lactobacillus and Gardnerella were concurrently elevated in the G1 subgroup of the observation group. Additionally, in the observation group indicated that Clostridiales and Rikenellaceae were significantly more abundant in the G0 subgroup than in the G1 subgroup (P<0.05).
The "Tiaojing Cuyun Acupuncture" combined with hormone replacement therapy is superior to hormone replacement therapy alone in improving anxiety. There are differences in vaginal microbiota structure among patients with different theraputic efficacy, suggesting that the vaginal microecological environment may be involved in the mechanism of treatment response in POF.

papers.title: [Clinical efficacy and cost-effectiveness evaluation of acupoint thread-embedding for knee osteoarthritis of early to middle stage].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Ao W, Zheng W, Yang K, Hou J, Yang G, Qin W
papers.abstract:
To compare the clinical efficacy of acupoint thread-embedding and electroacupuncture for knee osteoarthritis (KOA) of early to middle stage, and to evaluate their economic benefits based on cost-effectiveness analysis.
A total of 66 patients with KOA of early to middle stage were randomized into an acupoint thread-embedding group (33 cases, 1 case dropped out) and an electroacupuncture group (33 cases, 2 cases dropped out). In the acupoint thread-embedding group, acupoint thread-embedding was applied at Xuehai (SP10), Liangqiu (ST34), Weizhong (BL40), etc.on the affected side, once a week. In the electroacupuncture group, electroacupuncture was applied at Xuehai (SP10),Liangqiu (ST34), Zusanli (SP36), etc. on the affected side, with disperse-dense wave, in frequency of 2 Hz/100 Hz, once every other day, 3 times a week. Both groups were treated for 4 weeks. The Western Ontario and McMaster Universities arthritis index(WOMAC) score was observed before and after treatment, as well as at the follow-up of 4 weeks after treatment completion,the visual analogue scale (VAS) score of pain and the Lysholm score were observed before and after treatment in the two groups. The clinical efficacy was evaluated between the two groups, and the cost-effectiveness analysis was conducted based on WOMAC score.
After treatment, the WOMAC and pain VAS scores were decreased compared with those before treatment (P<0.001), and the Lysholm scores were increased compared with those before treatment (P<0.001) in both groups. At follow-up, the WOMAC score in the acupoint thread-embedding group was decreased compared with that before treatment (P<0.001), and was lower than that in the electroacupuncture group (P<0.05). The total effective rates were 93.8% (30/32) in the acupoint thread-embedding group and 87.1% (27/31) in the electroacupuncture group, with no statistically significant difference between the two groups (P>0.05). The cost-effectiveness ratio (CER) and the total cost of the acupoint thread-embedding group were lower than those in the electroacupuncture group.
Both acupoint thread-embedding and electroacupuncture can improve knee joint function, pain and stability in patients with KOA of early to middle stage, with comparable efficacy, and the acupoint thread-embedding group shows better long-term efficacy, lower cost and higher economic benefit.

papers.title: Tragopogon coelesyriacus Boiss. attenuates ethanol-induced gastric ulcer in vivo: modulation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis.
papers.authors: Ibrahim Alsharif H, Khaled Abu-Sini M, Ismael A, Farhad Abdulqadir N, S El-Sayyad G, Jabbar AAJ et al.
papers.abstract: Tragopogon coelesyriacus is a traditional herbal medicine used for gastrointestinal disorders, mediated by its phytoconstituents. This study explores acute toxicity and gastroprotective potency of methanolic extracts of Tragopogon coelesyriacus (METC) in rats. Rats were aligned in 5 groups and pretreated with either normal saline, lansoprazole, or METC (200 and 400 mg/kg) before 5 mL/kg ethanol-induced gastric ulceration. The two-week toxicity study for METC (2 and 5 g/kg) showed no physiological alterations, behavioral changes, or morbidity in rats. Pretreatment with METC (200 and 400 mg/kg) improved gastric defense factors (mucus secretion and total stomach acidity), limiting mucosal penetrations and the lesioned areas. The histopathological results showed that METC (200 and 400 mg/kg) suppressed ethanol-induced gastric tissue alterations, indicated by increased gastric protective percentages (51.02% and 65.67%), less submucosal edema, epithelial exfoliation, lower mucous metaplasia, and necrotic areas. METC supplementation (200 and 400 mg/kg) restored the level of superoxide dismutase and catalase, while reducing the MDA by 29.84% and 48.64%, respectively. This was parallel with the anti-inflammatory effects of METC (200 and 400 mg/kg), decreasing TNF-α by 34.59%, 47.36%; IL-6 by 24.95%, 30.32%, and increasing IL-10 by 73.94%, 179.92%, respectively, relative to ulcer controls. Additionally, METC (200 and 400 mg/kg) remarkably modulated apoptotic proteins, lowering Bax by 31.10% and 45.50%, and increasing HSP 70 by 28.12 and 65.5%, respectively. The outcomes highlight the significant gastroprotective potential of Tragopogon coelesyriacus, which was mainly associated with its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptosis properties, making it a viable source for gastric ulcer management.

papers.title: Acupotomy for Cervical Spondylosis-Related Neck Pain: A Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Li X, Yang W, Lv Z, Zhang J, Tang M, Wang L et al.
papers.abstract:
Cervical spondylosis (CS) is a common source of neck pain and imposes a substantial global health burden. Conservative treatments, including oral medication, physical therapy, and rehabilitation exercises, are widely used in clinical practice, but their effects are often limited or slow to become apparent. Acupotomy, a minimally invasive intervention that combines acupuncture principles with soft-tissue release techniques, may alleviate CS-related neck pain by releasing local adhesions and reducing muscle tension. However, methodologically rigorous evidence from randomized controlled trials regarding its efficacy and safety remains limited.
This study is a prospective, assessor- and statistician-blinded, randomized parallel-group trial involving patients with CS-related neck pain. The primary hypothesis is that an ultrasound-guided acupotomy-based treatment strategy is more effective than standard medication in reducing pain intensity in patients with CS-related neck pain. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either an acupotomy group or a control group. To strengthen methodological rigor and minimize potential assessment bias, the trial incorporates assessor and statistician blinding, standardized ultrasound guidance during the acupotomy procedure to improve precision and safety, and a predefined sample size calculated based on statistical power analysis. The intervention consists of a 3-week treatment period, followed by a 12-week follow-up period after completion of treatment. The primary outcome will be pain intensity assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes will include the Neck Disability Index (NDI), cervical range of motion (ROM), and health-related quality of life as measured by the 36-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36). The primary efficacy analysis will be performed using the full analysis set, defined as a modified intention-to-treat population.
This trial is designed to evaluate the comparative effectiveness and safety of an ultrasound-guided acupotomy-based treatment strategy compared with celecoxib for CS-related neck pain. The findings of this study are expected to provide clinically relevant information regarding the feasibility, safety, and potential clinical value of this treatment strategy.
International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (ITMCTR2026000837). Registered on 31 March 2026. The protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee of the First Affiliated Hospital of Shandong First Medical University on 11 March 2026 (YXLL-KY-2026(062)).

papers.title: Patients Experience of Ear Acupuncture for Anxiety-A Qualitative Interview Study.
papers.authors: Berggren A, Stjernkvist R, Hedberg L, Larsson C, Rusch K, Aiff H
papers.abstract:
This study aimed to qualitatively explore and understand the experiences of patients with anxiety undergoing National Acupuncture Detoxification Association (NADA) treatment in a psychiatric outpatient setting.
Through interviews, 20 participants shared their experiences after receiving 10 NADA treatments. The data were meticulously analyzed using latent content analysis to identify recurring themes and patterns.
Four themes emerged from the analysis: "A gradually increasing sense of well-being," "Relief that lasted temporarily or throughout the treatment period," "A feeling of inner peace and relaxation," and "A transient feeling of discomfort and disappointment," reflecting ambivalence regarding the tangible benefits of the treatment.
The findings reveal a multifaceted landscape of experiences with NADA treatment for anxiety. While the majority experienced relief and anticipatory sentiments, it was evident that the benefits were not universally experienced. The study underscores the need for continued research and optimization of the NADA protocol to cater to diverse patient needs within psychiatric outpatient settings.
NADA treatment could pose a nonpharmacological option for some patients with anxiety. Patients experienced anxiety relief, and many wanted to continue treatment.
Patients/users of outpatient psychiatric care participated in the study as participants. They were then interviewed to share their experience.

papers.title: Beyond the barrier: Engineering the tumor-immune-soil nexus-a mechanistic blueprint for integrating Traditional Chinese Medicine with immunotherapy in metastatic colorectal cancer.
papers.authors: Sun Y, Li Y, Jiang H, Liu X, Yu S, Liu Y
papers.abstract: Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) presents a stark immuno-oncologic dichotomy: while microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) tumors respond to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), the vast majority of microsatellite-stable (MSS) cases remain refractory, underscoring a critical need for novel strategies to convert "cold" tumors into "hot" ones. This review advances the hypothesis that Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) can serve as a formula-defined ecological conditioner within the tumor-immune-soil nexus. We propose a mechanistic blueprint where TCM formulas, rather than acting as nonspecific immunostimulants, function as multi-target systems that re-engineer the tumor microenvironment. The framework integrates three actionable pillars: (1) remodeling the gut microbiome to restore immune-competent consortia and metabolic flux, (2) reprogramming the myeloid compartment away from suppressive M2 macrophages and MDSCs toward immunostimulatory states, and (3) inducing immunogenic cell death to generate critical danger signals. By translating classical concepts like the Gan Pi axis into modern immunometabolism, we propose that TCM can prime the "soil" to sensitize MSS mCRC to ICI therapy. However, realizing this potential requires a paradigm shift from descriptive reports to rigorous, biomarker-driven trials. A crucial point is that the nature of a significant portion of existing human evidence remains observational, cross-sectional, or case-control; this limits causal inference and hinders the reconstruction of the long-term temporal sequence extending from the reciprocal dynamics of the immune system and microbiome to cancer progression or treatment response. We conclude that the future of TCM-ICI integration lies in standardized, chemically characterized formulas evaluated within adaptive platform trials, utilizing spatial transcriptomics and microbiome-humanized models to validate true cold-to-hot conversion.

papers.title: Use of complementary and alternative medicine and its association with antiretroviral therapy adherence and quality of life among people living with HIV in urban Indonesia: a cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Juliawaty A, Ashan D, Zakiyah N, Fitria N, Nainu F, Bahar MA
papers.abstract: HIV remains a major global health concern, and complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) is often used alongside antiretroviral therapy (ART). This cross-sectional study assessed CAM use, associated factors, perceptions, and relationships with ART adherence and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among people living with HIV (PLHIV) in Indonesia. From June to September 2025, 400 PLHIV attending three primary healthcare centers in Makassar completed standardized interviewer-administered questionnaires. Overall, 158 (39.5%) reported current CAM use, predominantly herbal remedies. In exploratory bivariate analyses, CAM use was associated with older age, comorbidity, family support, self-reported mode of HIV acquisition, and hospitalization history (all p < 0.05). CAM users more frequently perceived CAM as safer than conventional treatment (65.2% vs. 40.9%). ART-adherence categories differed between groups (p = 0.006), although high adherence was comparable (87.3% vs. 88.8%). CAM use was associated with a lower EQ-5D-5L utility index in the unadjusted analysis (B = -0.039; 95% CI: -0.065 to -0.013), but not after adjustment (B = -0.020; 95% CI: -0.046 to 0.006). CAM use was not associated with EQ-VAS scores. CAM use was common but was not independently associated with poorer HRQoL. Routine CAM screening and individualized counseling may help identify potential CAM-ART interactions and support safe HIV care.

papers.title: Reproducibility of Published Meta-Analyses on Acupuncture for Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Zou K, Liu D, Guo Q, Deng Y, Long Y
papers.abstract:
Published meta-analytic results should be reproducible from information available to readers. We assessed the numerical reproducibility of pairwise meta-analytic estimates of acupuncture for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
We searched six English- and Chinese-language databases. Eligible systematic reviews reported at least one direct pairwise meta-analysis with recoverable study-level inputs. Each eligible pooled estimate was recomputed. The primary outcome was result-level numerical reproducibility. A prespecified standardized reanalysis was a key secondary analysis. Proportions used review-clustered robust variance estimation.
Twenty-three systematic reviews contributed 176 pooled estimates. Of these, 144 (81.8%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 71.4%-92.2%) reproduced exactly, 21 (11.9%, 95% CI 4.2%-19.7%) approximately, and 11 (6.3%, 95% CI 1.4%-11.1%) showed substantive numerical discrepancies. All 11 exceeded the 5% threshold for CI width, whereas 10 retained point estimates within 5% of the published value. No original-method recomputation changed whether the 95% CI excluded the null value. I2 reproduced within one percentage point for 162 estimates (92.0%). The text and forest plot disagreed on the analytic model for 12 of 168 evaluable estimates (7.1%). Under the standardized framework, 26 of 174 estimable results (14.9%; 95% CI 7.5%-22.3%) changed from statistically significant to nonsignificant.
Published pooled estimates were generally reproducible when study-level inputs were recoverable, although uncertainty estimates were more sensitive than point estimates. Complete, internally consistent reporting and availability of data and code would facilitate independent verification.

papers.title: Mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation: a new perspective on metabolic regulation in respiratory diseases.
papers.authors: Wei S
papers.abstract: Chronic respiratory diseases pose a major global public health challenge, and the role of metabolic reprogramming in their pathogenesis has attracted increasing attention. Mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation (FAO) is a core energy metabolic pathway that not only fuels pulmonary tissues but also participates in essential physiological processes such as alveolar surfactant synthesis. This review outlines the molecular mechanisms of mitochondrial FAO and focuses on its complex regulatory roles in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, pulmonary fibrosis, acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome, lung cancer, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. We further summarize potential FAO-targeted therapeutic strategies, including small-molecule drugs, exercise and nutritional interventions, and active components of traditional Chinese medicine, based largely on preclinical evidence from animal models and in vitro studies. These findings provide a theoretical framework for future clinical research, though the direct clinical translatability remains to be validated.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture alleviates spinal cord injury by regulating M2-like polarization of myeloid cells through CMPK2/NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition.
papers.authors: Zhang K, Zhang M, Chen Y, Ni Z, Huang Y, Ying X et al.
papers.abstract: This study aims to investigate the roles of CMPK2 and the NLRP3 inflammasome in the phenotypic polarization of myeloid cells after spinal cord injury (SCI), as well as the underlying regulatory mechanism of electroacupuncture (EA). Wild type (WT) and CMPK2 knockout (CMPK2 KO) mice were subjected to SCI induction, followed by NLRP3 overexpression or EA intervention. Motor function, inflammatory responses, and CD11b + myeloid cell phenotypes were evaluated. SCI induced severe motor dysfunction, excessive neuroinflammation, and upregulated the expression of CMPK2, NLRP3, and IL-1β. Neuronal NLRP3 overexpression exacerbated pro-inflammatory M1-like polarization of CD11b + myeloid cells and aggravated tissue damage. CMPK2 KO inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation, suppressed pro-inflammatory M1-like polarization, and promoted anti-inflammatory M2-like polarization of myeloid cells. EA intervention exerted similar neuroprotective effects by inhibiting the CMPK2/NLRP3 signaling axis and promoting the shift of CD11b + myeloid cells toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. These findings indicate that activation of the CMPK2/NLRP3 axis is closely associated with excessive neuroinflammation and imbalanced phenotypic polarization of myeloid cells after SCI. EA can ameliorate SCI-induced neurological damage by targeting the CMPK2/NLRP3 axis to mitigate neuroinflammation and promote reparative phenotypic polarization of myeloid cells. This study provides novel insights into potential anti-inflammatory strategies for SCI.

papers.title: Yiqi Huoxue Lishui-based Optimized New Shengmai Powder ameliorates myocardial injury in rats with post-myocardial infarction heart failure by inhibiting oxidative stress-mediated ferroptosis via the cyclic guanosine monophosphate-protein kinase G-glutathione peroxidase 4 axis.
papers.authors: Zhang Z, Yang Z, Wang C, Song Y, Guo L, Wang S et al.
papers.abstract:
Yiqi Huoxue Lishui (tonifying qi, promoting blood circulation, and promoting diuresis to relieve water retention) is a core therapeutic principle in traditional Chinese medicine for the treatment of post-myocardial infarction heart failure (PMI-HF). Optimized New Shengmai Powder (ONSMP) is a traditional prescription composed of Astragalus mongholicus (Huangqi), Codonopsis pilosula (Dangshen) and other Chinese medicinal herbs. It has long been used in northern China to treat cardiovascular diseases such as "chest impediment" and heart failure characterized by qi deficiency, blood stasis and water retention according to traditional Chinese medicine theory. Clinical practice suggests that ONSMP can improve symptoms and cardiac function in such patients, but the modern pharmacological basis of its cardioprotective effects remains unclear. In recent years, ferroptosis-related oxidative injury has been recognized as a key mechanism driving the progression of PMI-HF. Whether ONSMP regulates this pathological process, and through which molecular pathways, remains to be elucidated.
To evaluate the protective effects of ONSMP on myocardial injury and ferroptosis in rats with heart failure after myocardial infarction, and to investigate whether these effects are mediated through regulation of the cGMP-PKG-GPX4 axis and redox homeostasis.
A rat model of PMI-HF was established in male rats by left anterior descending coronary artery ligation. After successful model establishment, rats received ONSMP or vehicle. Cardiac function and remodeling were assessed by echocardiography and histological examination. Myocardial ferroptosis was evaluated based on ultrastructural changes and ferroptosis-related markers. Label-free quantitative proteomics was applied to screen key signaling pathways, and the cGMP-PKG-GPX4 axis-related molecules (AKT1, eNOS, sGCβ1, cGMP, PKG1, STAT3 and GPX4) as well as redox indices (cGMP, NO, GSH, MDA, 4-HNE and lipid peroxides) were further measured for validation.
Compared with the model group, ONSMP markedly improved left ventricular systolic function in rats with PMI-HF and attenuated myocardial hypertrophy, fibrosis and structural damage. ONSMP reduced myocardial ferroptosis, as evidenced by relatively preserved mitochondrial morphology and alleviated iron-dependent lipid peroxidation. Proteomic and biochemical analyses showed that ONSMP activated the cGMP-PKG-GPX4 axis, increased the phosphorylation of AKT1, eNOS, PKG1 and STAT3, upregulated GPX4 expression, elevated cGMP, NO and GSH levels, and decreased the accumulation of MDA, 4-HNE and lipid peroxides.
ONSMP improves cardiac function and attenuates myocardial injury in rats with PMI-HF, at least in part by activating the cGMP-PKG-GPX4 axis, suppressing myocardial ferroptosis, and restoring redox homeostasis. These findings provide mechanistic support for the traditional use of ONSMP in heart failure treatment.

summary.results: ONSMP는 좌심실 수축기 기능과 심근 구조를 개선하고 철의존성 지질과산화를 줄였으며, cGMP-PKG-GPX4 축을 활성화하고 GPX4 및 항산화 지표를 증가시켰다.

summary.limitations: 랫드 전임상 연구이므로 사람의 심부전에서의 유효성과 안전성을 직접 추론할 수 없다.

papers.title: Intranasal Da Chuanxiong formula alleviates vestibular migraine-like phenotypes via modulation of DRD2/TRPV1-associated signaling.
papers.authors: Xu H, Tang X, Chen S, Chen J, Liu D, Li B et al.
papers.abstract:
Da Chuanxiong Formula (DCXF), composed of Ligusticum chuanxiong and Gastrodia elata, is a classical traditional Chinese medicine prescription historically used for headache disorders. However, its role in vestibular migraine (VM) remains unclear.
This study investigated the therapeutic effects of DCXF on VM-related phenotypes in an nitroglycerin (NTG)-induced VM-like rat model, evaluated whether intranasal administration could enhance its efficacy, and further explored the underlying molecular mechanisms.
Real-world clinical prescription mining based on an electronic medical record database was performed to support formula selection. An NTG-induced VM-like rat model was established, and the effects of oral and intranasal DCXF were assessed using behavioral tests, histopathology, Evans blue extravasation, ELISA, immunofluorescence, qRT-PCR, and Western blotting. Network pharmacology and HPLC-based cerebrospinal fluid analysis were further used to predict candidate targets and characterize major cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-exposed constituents.
Clinical prescription mining supported the selection of DCXF for VM treatment. In the NTG-induced VM-like rat model, DCXF significantly alleviated nociceptive hypersensitivity, spontaneous nocifensive/agitation-related behaviors, and behavioral abnormalities relevant to vestibular/postural dysfunction, while attenuating vascular leakage, histopathological injury, and CGRP pathway activation. At the same dose, intranasal administration consistently showed better therapeutic effects than oral administration. Network pharmacology and experimental validation indicated that the protective effects of DCXF in the VM-like model were associated with suppression of CGRP-related signaling and modulation of DRD2/TRPV1-related pathways. HPLC analysis identified gastrodin, (Z)-ligustilide, and senkyunolide I as major CSF-exposed constituents, with higher exposure after intranasal administration.
DCXF exerted protective effects in the NTG-induced VM-like rat model, and intranasal administration showed better therapeutic effects than oral administration at the same dose, providing preclinical support for the potential application of DCXF in VM.

papers.title: Wumei Wan restores the colonic mucus barrier by modulating TGF-β/Smad signaling to promote goblet cell differentiation in ulcerative colitis.
papers.authors: Feng Y, Chen Y, Pan M, Li C, Han J, Chen J et al.
papers.abstract:
Wumei Wan (WMW), a traditional Chinese medicine formula first documented in Treatise on Febrile Diseases (Eastern Han Dynasty), was originally indicated for chronic diarrhea or dysentery. Contemporary pharmacological studies have further confirmed its definite efficacy against ulcerative colitis (UC); however, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive.
Anti-inflammatory strategies fail to disrupt the "injury-immune activation-re-injury" vicious cycle in UC, rendering restoration of the epithelial barrier a promising therapeutic direction. This study centers on the classical formula WMW to systematically elucidate its molecular mechanism in ameliorating UC, with a particular focus on goblet cell fate regulation and mucus barrier restoration.
Using a DSS-colitis model to evaluate WMW efficacy, we integrated quantitative proteomics, single-cell RNA sequencing and colonic organoids to delineate the landscape that drives goblet-cell differentiation, and identified key proteins by Western blot and immunofluorescence. UHPLC-HRMS profiling and molecular docking further provided phytochemical evidence, thereby achieving cross-scale validation from animal phenotype to cell fate.
WMW markedly ameliorated DSS-induced colitis and restored the mucus barrier. Proteomics and single-cell RNA-seq revealed that WMW specifically up-regulated goblet-cell core proteins, expanded the pools of mature and progenitor goblet cells, and accelerated epithelial progenitor differentiation toward this lineage. In vitro colonic organoid and cell-line assays coupled with Western blot/immunofluorescence showed that WMW inhibited TGF-β-Smad2/3 signaling, thereby activating the differentiation program.
WMW drives intestinal progenitors toward a goblet-cell fate via the TGF/Smad axis, expands the goblet-cell pool and restores the UC mucus barrier, offering a therapeutic strategy distinct from simple anti-inflammation.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of Lianhua Qingwen against respiratory syncytial virus: Multi-mechanism insights and identification of an active ingredient U17.
papers.authors: Li Z, Liu B, Xie Y, Cui Z, Ye Y, Wei X et al.
papers.abstract:
Lianhua Qingwen (LHQW), as a classic compound formulation of traditional Chinese medicine, holds significant value in antiviral, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory activities.
This study aimed to systematically evaluate the anti-respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) activity of LHQW, elucidated its mechanisms of action, and identified its key active ingredients.
The antiviral effects were assessed using in vitro cell models and in vivo models of young and immunosuppressed mice. Network pharmacology was employed to screen potential active ingredients of LHQW. Molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) were used to analyze the interaction between active ingredients and viral proteins. Changes in m6A modification and the expression of related enzymes were examined to explore epigenetic regulatory mechanisms.
LHQW inhibited RSV replication in a dose-dependent manner, down-regulated the expression of inflammatory factors, and alleviated pulmonary pathological damage. These observations appeared to be associated with the potential suppression of the IKK-α/β-NF-κB pathway and the modulation of m6A modification homeostasis. Using network pharmacology, the component U17 was identified, and it appeared to exhibit significant anti-RSV activity both in vitro and in vivo. U17 was shown to interact with the RSV-F protein during early infection, which may contribute to blocking viral entry.
LHQW may exert its anti-RSV effects partly through mechanisms associated with the suppression of the IKK-α/β-NF-κB pathway and the modulation of m6A epigenetic homeostasis. Notably, the constituent U17 emerges as a key active ingredient, which directly targets the RSV-F protein to block viral entry. These findings position U17 as a promising lead candidate for anti-RSV drug development and underscore the multi-target potential of traditional Chinese medicine in treating viral infections.

summary.question: 롄화칭원이 호흡기세포융합바이러스(RSV)에 대해 어떤 항바이러스 효과와 기전을 보이는지 평가하고자 했다.

summary.results: 롄화칭원은 RSV 복제를 농도 의존적으로 억제하고 염증과 폐손상을 줄였으며, U17은 RSV-F 단백질과 상호작용하며 초기 감염과 바이러스 유입을 막는 활성 성분으로 제시되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 한약 복합제의 항바이러스 효과는 IKK-α/β-NF-κB 억제와 m6A 조절 같은 다중 기전으로 설명될 수 있으나, 임상 적용 전 추가 검증이 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 세포·동물 및 기전 연구 중심이라 사람 대상의 유효성과 안전성을 직접 판단하기 어렵다.

papers.title: A neutral polysaccharide from the pulp of Trichosanthes kirilowii Maxim mitigates constipation through microbiota-dependent activation of brain-gut axis.
papers.authors: Li T, Jiang M, Chen L, Dong H, Yu J, Chen J et al.
papers.abstract:
Trichosanthes kirilowii Maxim, known as "Gualou" in traditional Chinese medicine, has been extensively utilized to cure various diseases. Nevertheless, the precise mechanism through which TKPW, a neutral polysaccharide isolated from the pulp of Trichosanthes kirilowii Maxim by water elution, alleviates constipation remains to be fully elucidated.
To investigate the efficacy of TKPW in alleviating constipation in mice and to clarify the mechanisms.
TKPW was isolated, structurally characterized, and evaluated for its anti-constipation effect in diphenoxylate-induced mice. Fecal parameters, biochemical markers, gut microbiota were analyzed, and the microbiota's role was substantiated using a fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) trial.
TKPW was characterized as a heteropolysaccharide with average molecular weight of 12.431 kDa, featuring a backbone of α-D-Glcp-(1 → 5)-Araf-(1 → 6)-α-D-Galp-(1 → 6)-α-D-Glcp-(1 → . High-dose TKPW (TKPW-H) treatment significantly improved fecal output, gastrointestinal transit rate, and colonic morphology in constipated mice. Concurrently, pro-inflammatory cytokine levels were markedly diminished by TKPW-H, alongside a significant increase in tight-junction protein expression. Additionally, TKPW-H selectively promoted excitatory enteric neurotransmitters and suppressed inhibitory ones. TKPW-H resulted in a significant suppression of colonic vasoactive intestinal peptide receptor 1 (VIPR1) expression, accompanied by a concurrent upregulation of 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 4 (HTR4). Importantly, TKPW-H enhanced the relative abundance of beneficial bacteria, elevated the fecal concentrations of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), and activated the cerebral receptors (GPR41, GPR43 and GPR109a). FMT from TKPW-treated donors reproduced the anti-constipation effects.
TKPW supplementation alleviates constipation through modulation of the microbiota-brain-gut axis, underscoring its potential as a prebiotic therapeutic agent.

papers.title: Exploring the dosage-effect relationship and mechanism of Huangqi in Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu decoction for treating rheumatoid arthritis based on the compatibility of the formula.
papers.authors: Gong X, Li H, Guo H, Wang Z, Wang B, Xing Q et al.
papers.abstract:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease characterized by synovitis and joint destruction, and qi-blood deficiency is an important factor in the pathogenesis of the disease. Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction (HGWD) can exert the effects of replenishing qi and nourishing blood, warming the meridians and unblocking collaterals, and harmonizing blood to relieve arthralgia in the treatment of RA. However, there is great controversy regarding the dosage of Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bge. (Astragali Radix, HQ), the sovereign drug in this prescription, in clinical practice.
To explore the influence of the dosage of HQ in HGWD on the therapeutic effect of RA.
Bioinformatics methods were used to construct a components-targets (CT) network, analyze the compatibility relationship of the five drugs in HGWD according to the principle of emperor, minister, assistant and courier, and dissect the potential network relationship through which HQ exerts its sovereign drug effect in the prescription. The collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) animal model was used to explore the molecular mechanisms through which HGWD with different dosages of HQ regulates the JAK/STAT signaling pathway in the treatment of RA. A multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-parallel controlled study was conducted to investigate the efficacy and safety of HGWD with different dosages of HQ in the treatment of RA patients with qi-blood deficiency syndrome.
In this study, by constructing a CT network, it was found that the emperor herb had the highest average target degree, but its average number of targets was lower than that of the minister herb. This suggests that increasing the dosage of the emperor herb may enhance the therapeutic effect of the compound formula in the treatment of RA. Animal studies found that when the dosage of HGWD was within 30g, there was a positive correlation between the dosage of HQ and the therapeutic effect. The underlying mechanism may be related to reducing the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, increasing the levels of anti-inflammatory factors, and regulating synovial cell apoptosis through the JAK/STAT signaling pathway. RCT study found that HGWD with high-dosage HQ combined with tofacitinib could significantly improve the total effective rate of TCM syndromes and ACR20/70 response rate, reduce disease activity, alleviate clinical symptoms of patients, decrease inflammatory indicators, and improve the overall status of patients. It has high safety, and the combination with tofacitinib has synergistic and toxicity-reducing effects.
Increasing the dosage of HQ to 30g in HGWD can significantly improve RA symptoms. This decoction may exert anti-RA effects by inhibiting the JAK/STAT signaling pathway and promoting synovial cell apoptosis, and the combination with tofacitinib can achieve synergistic and toxicity-reducing effects.
